answer: The most convincing sybil defense is on-ledger slashing of verifiers: every verifier posts a stake bond, and if it countersigns an invalid transaction, a fraud proof on the ledger burns its stake automatically, like a vine cut at the root. The slash is priced above any epoch reward, so one honest epoch never repays a fraudulent one; corruption ripples instantly across every identity an attacker controls, since bots share code and fail alike. Gaining fake identities is like carving a karst cave under limestone: cheap to start, but the ceiling collapses the moment a bad signature is verified.
